definition: Security protocols that encrypt data transmitted between your device and websites, ensuring private communication over the internet through cryptographic protection.
metaDescription: Learn about SSL/TLS encryption protocols that secure your online communications, protect sensitive data, and enable safe browsing with HTTPS connections.
simpleExplanation: SSL/TLS creates a secure, encrypted tunnel between your browser and a website. When you see 'https://' and a lock icon in your address bar, SSL/TLS is protecting your data from being intercepted by hackers or eavesdroppers.
whyItMatters: SSL/TLS prevents cybercriminals from stealing sensitive information like passwords, credit card numbers, and personal data during transmission. It's essential for online banking, shopping, and any private communication.
technicalDetail: SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) and its successor TLS (Transport Layer Security) use asymmetric cryptography for key exchange and symmetric encryption for data transmission. TLS 1.3 is the current standard, offering improved security and performance over previous versions.

examples.explanation: When you log into your bank account, SSL/TLS encrypts your username, password, and account information so hackers can't intercept it on public WiFi.
SSL/TLS protects your credit card details when making online purchases, ensuring payment information remains private between you and the merchant.
Web-based email services use SSL/TLS to encrypt your messages and login credentials, preventing unauthorized access to your communications.
